lessons.title: What Would You Like?

items.meaning: I would like a window seat.
items.exampleMeaning: I would like a window seat.

items.text: Ich möchte ein Ticket nach Berlin.
items.meaning: I would like a ticket to Berlin.
items.example: Ich möchte ein Ticket nach Berlin.
items.exampleMeaning: I would like a ticket to Berlin.

items.text: Ich hätte gerne einen Platz am Gang.
items.meaning: I would like an aisle seat.
items.example: Ich hätte gerne einen Platz am Gang.
items.exampleMeaning: I would like an aisle seat.

items.meaning: I would like the boarding pass.
items.exampleMeaning: I would like the boarding pass.

lessons.tip: Use 'möchte' to express what you would like. It is a polite way to ask for something.

scenario.brief: Ask the passenger what they would like. Offer options like a window seat or an upgrade.

lessons.title: Travel Documents

items.meaning: I have my passport with me.
items.exampleMeaning: I have my passport with me.

items.meaning: I am looking for my boarding pass.
items.exampleMeaning: I am looking for my boarding pass.

lessons.tip: Use 'haben' to indicate possession. It is important to show what you have when traveling.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Do you have your passport?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, ich habe meinen Reisepass dabei.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I have my passport with me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Where is your ticket?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: I am looking for my ticket.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Could you help me?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I have everything.

scenario.partnerRole: An airport staff member checking documents.
scenario.brief: Ask the passenger for their travel documents. Help them if they cannot find something.
scenario.goal: You need to show your travel documents.

lessons.title: Asking Questions

items.text: Wie viel kostet das Ticket nach München?
items.meaning: How much is the ticket to Munich?
items.example: Wie viel kostet das Ticket nach München?
items.exampleMeaning: How much is the ticket to Munich?

lessons.tip: Use 'wie viel', 'wann', 'wo' to ask questions about prices, times, and locations. These words help you get information.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Wie viel kostet das Ticket nach München?
dialogue.meaning: How much is the ticket to Munich?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: The ticket costs one hundred euros.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: When does the plane leave?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Das Flugzeug fliegt um drei Uhr.
dialogue.meaning: The plane leaves at three o'clock.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Where is the gate?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: The gate is over there.

scenario.partnerRole: An airport staff member answering questions.
scenario.brief: Ask the passenger questions about their flight and ticket. Provide clear answers.
scenario.goal: You need to ask questions about your flight.

lessons.title: Final Preparation

items.meaning: I am looking forward to the trip.

items.exampleMeaning: I am looking forward to the trip.

items.meaning: I hope it will be good.
items.exampleMeaning: I hope it will be good.

lessons.tip: Use 'ich bin' to express your state or feelings. It is a basic way to talk about yourself.

scenario.partnerRole: An airport staff member doing final checks.
